title: An Evaluation of the Effect of Network Cost Optimization for Leadership Class Supercomputers
problem: Dragonfly-based networks achieve cost savings through reduced cable lengths and switch counts, but impose tradeoffs including reduced global minimal paths and tapered topology resulting in less bisection bandwidth compared to fat-tree networks. The impact of these cost optimizations on exascale capability workloads remains empirically unquantified.
motivation: Three US Exascale supercomputers will deploy dragonfly networks, making empirical evaluation of their performance and cost-effectiveness critical for the HPC community.
method: Large-scale empirical evaluation comparing Frontier (dragonfly-based exascale system) to Summit (fat-tree-based previous generation system), using synthetic microbenchmarks, mini-apps, and full-scale applications to measure scaling efficiencies across diverse communication patterns.
key_novelty: First large-scale empirical evaluation of dragonfly topology at exascale scale, quantifying the performance impact of network cost optimizations on capability workloads.
contributions: First empirical evaluation of dragonfly network at exascale scale on Frontier supercomputer
Quantification of cost-efficiency: dragonfly networks achieve ~30% cost savings versus fat-tree, amortizing to ~3% of total exascale system cost
Demonstration that tapered dragonfly impacts are workload-dependent, primarily affecting all-to-all collective operations and latency-sensitive nearest-neighbor communication
Comprehensive performance characterization using microbenchmarks, mini-apps, and production applications

metrics.speedup: Scaling efficiency comparison between dragonfly and fat-tree systems
metrics.other: Cost efficiency - dragonfly ~30% more cost-efficient than fat-tree; amortizes to ~3% of exascale system cost

limitations: Evaluation limited to two specific systems; results may not generalize to other network topologies or architectural variants beyond those tested.
primary_theme: Network topology trade-offs in exascale HPC systems
